subject: Throughput sizing follow-up - Finex
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finex.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + sizing asks (Finex)

Thanks again for the time earlier — good call. Quick recap of the performance/SLO requirements and the follow ups we agreed on: 

- Target SLOs
  - First-token latency (streaming): <= 200 ms median, <= 450 ms 95th
  - End-to-end response for typical responses (<= 80 tokens): <= 600 ms 95th

- Workload characterization (your answers on the call):
  - Typical response size: ~80 tokens (avg), prompt ~40 tokens -> total ~120 tokens per request
  - Steady-state QPS: ~1,200 QPS
  - Expected peak bursts: up to ~8,000 QPS (short bursts, 5-15 minutes)
  - Concurrency: ~3,000 concurrent open streaming connections during peaks
  - Streaming: required (chunked SSE) — client expects first chunk within 250 ms

- Derived throughput (rough):
  - Steady-state tokens/sec: 1,200 QPS * 120 tokens = ~144,000 tokens/sec
  - Peak tokens/sec: 8,000 QPS * 120 tokens = ~960,000 tokens/sec

Next steps we agreed:
1) Alex/Priya to share 24-72h per-minute QPS export (CSV) showing steady vs burst windows + a few sample requests / response lengths.
2) We (Redwood) to produce a sizing recommendation (instance class + concurrency targets + caching/batching knobs) and cost estimate. See attached initial worksheet (finex_workload_summary.csv) and draft recommendation (redwood_sizing_recommendation.pdf).
3) Schedule a follow-up to review sizing and any security/compliance gating.

Notes/assumptions: model family not finalized — our sizing below assumes an autoregressive LLM of ~30-70B parameters (quantized) with streaming enabled. If you end up on a much larger model, we will re-run the kernel selection and capacity estimates.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: finex_workload_summary.csv, redwood_sizing_recommendation.pdf

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + sizing asks (Finex)

Thanks Rafael — this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying questions before we drop the full CSV: 

1) For concurrency: when you say ~3,000 concurrent streaming connections during peaks, is that concurrent inflight tokens or concurrent open SSE streams? We can provide both, but our client App keeps long-lived SSE connections for user sessions (many will be idle for stretches).
2) Burst profile: the 8k QPS is a 5-15 minute peak window — is the Redwood sizing doc assuming we rely mostly on autoscale (burst) vs reserved capacity? We need a cost estimate for both.
3) Model family: we will likely run a smaller instruct model for chat (Mistral-ish 34B equivalent) for most interactions and reserve a 70B model for high-fidelity risk-sensitive flows. Can your sizing doc show both variants?

We'll attach the per-minute QPS export and some sample payloads (will send by EOD Thu). One more ask: does Redwood support partial-response priority (i.e., deliver first chunk ASAP even if generation continues)? That's critical for our UX.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, Finex

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + sizing asks (Finex)

Alex — quick answers inline + updated ask.

1) Concurrency: we mean concurrent open SSE streams (your description is correct). Idle connections with no inflight tokens still count when provisioning for connection multiplexing; please indicate both counts if you can.
2) Autoscale vs reserved: our initial recommendation will include a baseline reserved pool sized for steady-state and a burst autoscale buffer. I’ll include two cost scenarios in the PDF: (A) Reserved-heavy (lower per-token cost, higher committed spend) and (B) Autoscale-first (pay-as-you-go, higher tail cost).
3) Model variants: yes — we will produce a dual-profile sizing: Mistral-34B class and Mistral-70B class (quantized). Each profile will include tokens/sec capacity, instance counts, and recommended batching/cache settings.

Also: Redwood supports prioritized partial responses. For streaming we can guarantee first-chunk delivery within the first-token latency SLO (provided the model and network path are similar to call assumptions).

Action items before the follow-up:
- You: send per-minute QPS export + example requests (EOD Thu / Aug 1 will work).
- Us: update sizing PDF with two model profiles, autoscale vs reserved scenarios, and a suggested canary rollout plan.

I'll target sending the updated sizing doc by Mon, Aug 3. If you can send the CSV by EOD Aug 1 it will let us validate against real peaks.

Rafael\n
Attachments: redwood_sizing_recommendation.pdf (draft)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finex.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + sizing asks (Finex)

Alex — quick technical note from eng/solutions: 

- If you can provide a 24-hour request log with the following columns we can run an automated sizing script and validate the PDF: timestamp, request_id, user_id (hashed ok), request_tokens, response_tokens, model_tag, connection_state (active/idle).
- For streaming semantics: chunk size is important. If your frontend expects char-level streaming we recommend 20-40 token chunks; if chunk latency is more important than chunk fidelity we can tune to 8-16 token chunks with some throughput loss.
- Also include a 95th-percentile HTTP/2 connection setup time if you have it (helps tune first-byte latency).

I can run an initial run and share the per-instance concurrency and token/sec numbers we expect.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Thanks everyone — we’ll get the CSV and sample payloads over to you by EOD tomorrow (Tue Aug 3). Plan to include the columns Marissa specified.

Alex
